artworks.title: Title Page for The Golden Scepter, by John Preston
artworks.description: This is a detailed engraving of the title page of a book titled "The Golden Scepter." The central rectangular area features the title of the book, "THE GOLDEN SCEPTER. with The Churches Marriage; And THE CHURCHES CARRIAGE. In three Treatises, BY The late Learned Divine, John Preston." Surrounding the central text are various intricate engravings. In the top left corner, one scene shows a kneeling individual receiving a scepter from an enthroned figure, accompanied by the text, "Then was I in his eyes as one that found favor." To the right, another scene depicts a king and a woman with the text, "I am my beloved's and my beloved is mine." Below, on the left, a group of figures is shown, with some appearing empathetic, and the words, "They have humbled themselves, therefore I will not destroy them." In the bottom right corner, an individual is depicted bending over a book, illuminated by a divine light, alongside the phrase, "When thou goest, it shall lead thee." The style is reminiscent of the detailed woodcut or metal engraving techniques from the 17th century, with intricate shading and texture created using hatching and cross-hatching.

artworks.title: Charles II as Prince
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a person from the chest up, facing slightly to their left. The individual, referred to as a prince, has long, curly hair reaching past the shoulders. They have an oval-shaped face with prominent features, including a pronounced nose and lips. The person wears a wide-brimmed hat with a large feather and a detailed jacket with light and dark vertical stripes. They have a high-collared lace shirt with a prominent lace edge. The figure is enclosed within an oval frame with surrounding text and a finely hatched background. The bottom of the image features a decorative border with text. The style resembles a classical engraving technique.

artworks.title: Algeron Percy, 10th Earl of Northumberland
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a person depicted from the waist up, positioned with their body slightly turned to the side while their head faces forward, looking directly at the viewer. The person has distinctive facial features with pronounced eyebrows, a well-groomed mustache, and long wavy hair that falls over the shoulders. They are dressed in a dark garment with a detailed, ruffled white collar. The person is encased within an ornate oval frame that bears inscriptions and decorative elements. Around this frame are additional embellishments, including the figure of a bearded man holding a trident and a seated figure of a woman. In the background, several ships sail on the sea under a cloud-filled sky.

artworks.title: Josuah Sylvester, Poet
artworks.description: The image shows an engraved portrait of a man from the chest up within an ornate oval frame. The man is positioned facing forward with his head slightly turned to his side, sporting well-defined facial features—a high forehead, strong brows, and a neatly trimmed beard and mustache. His hair is short and styled, adorned with a laurel wreath that encircles his head. He wears an elaborate ruffled collar and a richly detailed garment with intricate stitching and puffed sleeves. The background has a dense pattern, and around the oval frame is a decorative border with Latin text. Below the portrait are verses honoring the person's accomplishments and character, along with the name 'John Sturart' inscribed at the bottom.

artworks.title: Title Page to Cruso, Militarie Instructions for the Cavallrie
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a military scene featuring cavalry. The central focus is a large frame with the title "MILITARIE INSTRUCTIONS for the CAVALLRIE: According to the Moderne Warrs" in decorative script. Surrounding the title, cavalrymen on horseback are depicted in different formations or scenarios. Atop the frame is a decorative coat of arms with helmets, plumes, and military symbols. In the background, a view of a city or fortress is visible. The lower section shows a skirmish between two mounted soldiers, one holding a gun and the other a lance. The composition is detailed, emphasizing military instruction and cavalry maneuvers.

artworks.title: Patrick Forbes, Bishop of Aberdeen
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man from the chest up. He is facing forward with his head slightly turned to his right, gazing directly out of the frame. The man has facial hair and a neutral expression with gently arched eyebrows. His hair is neatly styled and he wears a decorated collared garment, possibly a ruff. The circular frame around the portrait has inscribed text and the background features fine, engraved lines. Below the portrait, there is more inscribed text. The overall style of the image suggests it is an engraving.

artworks.title: Richard Gethinge, Writing Master
artworks.description: The image depicts the upper part of a man's body within an ornate oval frame, labeled "RICHARDUS GETHING HERTFORDIENSIS ÆT. 32." The man is looking slightly to the left, showing his right profile. He has a neatly trimmed beard and mustache, curly closely cropped hair, and wears a detailed garment with a high collar and ruffles, as well as a buttoned jacket. To the right of the frame is an artistic representation of a hand holding a quill, suggesting writing or calligraphy. The background features calligraphic flourishes and text.

artworks.title: John Bate, Writer
artworks.description: The image shows an engraved portrait of a man facing forward with his head turned slightly to the right. The man has a wide nose, a short mustache, and his eyes are looking at the viewer. His hair is styled in a short wavy fringe and he is dressed in historical attire with a high collar and padded sleeves. The background features an oval frame with a cross-hatched pattern and below the oval, there is text that reads "Vera Effiges Johannis Bate: Memoria manet, modo permaneat Studium et industria."

artworks.title: John Bate
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man, focusing on his head and shoulders. The man is facing forward with a slight turn to his left. He has a mustache and short, curly hair. He is wearing a garment with a wide, stiff collar that is buttoned down in the front. The background of the portrait includes a finely lined oval frame. Text in elegant script is at the bottom of the image. There are no visible objects or jewelry.

artworks.title: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester
artworks.description: The image displays an engraving of a man seated from the waist up, facing forward with his arms on a cushion. His head is turned slightly to the left. The man has distinct facial features, including a long beard and high forehead. He wears a cap, a high-collared shirt, fur stole over his shoulders, and voluminous sleeves. He holds an open book in his hands on the cushion. The background is detailed with lines and patterns. Text at the bottom of the image contributes to its historical aesthetic.

artworks.title: Hugh Latimer
artworks.description: The image depicts a man seated at a desk with a book open in front of him. He has aged facial features, a long beard, and short hair, wearing a robe and a skullcap. The background is wooden-panelled, possibly in a study or library setting. An inscribed label appears at the bottom of the image. The scene is intricately detailed with engraved lines.

artworks.title: Lionel Lockyer, Physician
artworks.description: The image is an engraving of Lionel Lockyer, focusing on his bust. He is depicted facing forward with a calm expression, showcasing his facial features, long hair, and attire. The engraving is enclosed in an oval frame with his name and a poem inscribed below. The background consists of fine horizontal lines emphasizing the figure within the frame.

artworks.title: Nathaniel Richards, Dramatist
artworks.description: This image depicts a man from the waist up, seated or standing in a frontal position with his body slightly turned to one side. He has pronounced facial features with a full beard and mustache, shoulder-length wavy hair adorned with a laurel wreath. The man wears a detailed, patterned coat with a large white collar and holds a book or small rectangular object with both hands. The portrait is surrounded by an elaborate frame with text on banners, and the background features a scenic landscape with trees, hills, and a distant building.

artworks.title: Title Page to Juvenal's Satyrs, by Sir R. Stapleton
artworks.description: The image shows three figures in a detailed illustration. In the center is a person in a medallion-style frame, displaying the head and shoulders. The person has classical features with curly hair and laurel leaves, dressed in ancient Roman clothing and holding a small book or tablet. Flanking the central figure are two standing men in classical robes. The background features architectural elements and columns, evoking ancient Roman surroundings. Above, an eagle is perched on a pedestal adorned with a wreath and other classical ornaments. Text at the bottom specifies "JUVENALLS SATYRS" and the author Sir Robert Stapylton, Kt. Gent. of the Privy Chamber to the Prince, with decorative scrollwork and artistic embellishments.

artworks.title: Robert Aylett
artworks.description: The image is an engraved portrait of a man showing him from the waist up. He is positioned slightly sideways, with his head turned toward the viewer. The man has facial hair including a mustache and a pointed goatee. His hair is short and appears to be grey or light brown, neatly styled. He is wearing a formal outfit with a ruffled collar, a dark overcoat with decorative buttons. In his hand, he is holding a small rolled-up piece of paper. There is no visible jewelry. The background of the engraving has parallel lines on one side and a darker, stippled pattern on the other. There is a handwritten inscription and date at the top, and a Latin text below the image.

artworks.title: Robert Aylett
artworks.description: The image shows the upper half of a man's body. He is seated, holding a scroll. The man has a goatee, mustache, and short wavy hair. He wears a formal outfit with a large collar, buttons, and a pendant around his neck. The background has fine lines. There is script at the lower section and handwritten markings near the top left corner.

artworks.title: Francis Bacon
artworks.description: The image shows a man sitting at a writing desk, holding a quill in his right hand. He has a long face, a moustache, a goatee, shoulder-length wavy hair, and is wearing a large hat, a dark garment with intricate embroidery, a lace ruff, and puffed sleeves. On the desk are an open book and an inkpot with quills. The background shows a lined pattern, a coat of arms, books with Latin titles on a shelf, and text praising someone named Bacon.

artworks.title: Francis Lord Verulam Viscount St. Alban
artworks.artist: Thomas Cross after Crispijn de Passe I
artworks.description: The image depicts an engraving of a male figure from the waist up, seated and facing slightly to the right. The figure has a calm expression with gently arched eyebrows, a mustache, and a pointed beard. He has short wavy hair and wears a tall, rounded hat with a wide brim. The man is dressed in early 17th-century attire with a high lace ruff around the neck, a decorative doublet, and a cloak draped over his shoulders. He holds a small folded piece of paper in his right hand. The background consists of closely spaced horizontal lines, and there is an inscription at the bottom identifying him as Francis Lord Verulam Viscount St. Alban.

artworks.title: Francis Lord Verulam Viscount St. Alban
artworks.description: This image depicts a man from the torso up. He is seated with a straight posture, facing the viewer. The man has a defined face with a pointed chin and a mustache, and appears to have long, wavy hair. He is wearing a tall, dark hat and a lace ruff around his neck. His clothing is richly decorated with a pattern, and he holds a piece of paper in his right hand. The background consists of horizontal lines and the bottom of the image includes an inscription.

artworks.title: Tho. Browne, Med. Doctoris (Sir Thomas Browne, M.D.)
artworks.description: The image shows a portrait of a man with shoulder-length wavy dark hair, a mustache, and a small pointed beard. He is facing slightly to the right, making eye contact with the viewer. He has a neutral expression with distinct features and a slight curve to his eyebrows. The man is wearing a dark garment and a white shirt with a collar. There is a decorative brooch or fastening in the shape of a small bow at the center of the collar. The background includes a textured dark area on the left and an opening on the right revealing an abstract outdoor scene. Below the portrait is Latin text with a emblem in the center.

artworks.title: Richardi Brownlowe Armigeri
artworks.description: This image depicts an engraving of a man shown from just below the waist and up. He is seated, likely on a chair, and faces slightly to his left while gazing directly at the viewer. The man has a receding hairline with short hair at the sides and a neatly trimmed beard and mustache. He wears a dark, high-collared garment with elaborate detailing, including what appears to be a decorative ruff around his neck and ruffled cuffs. The garment is adorned with buttons down the front. In his right hand, he holds a rolled document. The background features numerous lines, with ornamented chair finials visible on either side of his head. At the bottom of the engraving, there is a text inscription.

artworks.title: Richardi Brownlowe Armigeri
artworks.description: The image shows an engraving of a man seated, displaying his upper body. He is facing slightly to his left with his gaze directed forward, giving a three-quarter profile view. The man has a distinct facial appearance, with a neatly trimmed beard and mustache. His hair is covered by a hat or cap fitting closely to his head. He wears a voluminous ruffled collar and a dark gown with intricate embroidery or patterned borders. In his left hand, he holds a rolled document, and in his right hand, there is a fan or a brush. The chair he sits on has two finials visible on either side at the top of the backrest. The background features a decorative pattern, possibly wood-paneled or wallpaper.

artworks.title: Richardi Brownlowe Armigeri
artworks.description: The image shows a seated male figure from the waist up. The man faces forward with a slightly turned head, looking at the viewer. He has a distinguished facial appearance, an aged face with a neatly trimmed beard and mustache. His hair is dark and closely cropped, partially covered by a hat. He wears an elaborately designed robe with a high, pleated white ruff around his neck and detailed sleeves. He holds a scroll in one hand on his lap, while the other hand rests on the chair's armrest. The chair has large finials on the corners, enhancing its ornate look. The background has closely spaced horizontal lines providing texture and depth.

artworks.title: Robertus Cottonus Bruceus (Sir Robert Cotton)
artworks.description: The image is a portrait showing the upper body of a man positioned to face forward. His facial features include a full beard and mustache, with curly hair styled neatly. He wears an elaborately large ruff collar and a textured garment that suggests formal attire. There are no visible accessories. The background features an oval frame with the inscription "ROBERTUS COTTONUS BRUCEUS," and is filled with a crosshatch pattern. Below the portrait is a text in Latin.
